summary.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q2 FY27: revenue up 2.9% QoQ to over Rs.2,580 Cr, EBITDAaL margin 48.6%, mobile net adds turned negative on tariff action and Northeast weather.
summary.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q2 FY27 revenue of over Rs.2,580 Crores, up about 2.9% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of over Rs.1,250 Crores at a 48.6% margin. Mobile ARPU rose to Rs.264, helped by one extra day and the pricing intervention, but the mobile customer base saw churn and negative subscriber additions, which management attributed mainly to the tariff action, quarter seasonality and adverse Northeast weather. Homes, offices and other businesses added 71,000 net adds and grew revenue about 3.7% QoQ. Operating FCF (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs.920 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs.1,575 Crores. The call was a combined Airtel and Hexacom webinar; Hexacom-specific Q&A was largely on churn, ARPU gap versus Airtel, and reported versus cash capex.

segments.name: Mobile
segments.commentary: Mobile ARPU Rs.264 with 29 million customer base; subscriber additions turned negative on churn after the pricing action and Northeast weather disruption. Mobile revenue grew about 2.7% QoQ per analyst calculation versus Airtel's 3.4%.

segments.name: Homes, offices and other businesses
segments.commentary: 71,000 net adds in the quarter, down from over 100,000 per quarter as cited by an analyst; revenue grew about 3.7% QoQ. Management said the slowdown reflects a correction of low-ARPU, quality-poor acquisitions and a shift to fiber-led growth.

guidance_outlook: Management said early signs of improvement in churn versus last quarter, with Q3 to be watched; a tailwind from Northeast recharge disruption is possible going into Q3, though no formal guidance was given.
Postpaid ARPU uplift from the tariff intervention broadly about Rs.50, expected to flow through to ARPU, less some possible access charges for international roaming users.
Access charges expected to remain slightly higher while home broadband grows fast; management advised reading the trailing 12-month trend rather than quarterly figures.
Management declined to give forward guidance on Hexacom's mobile growth relative to Airtel.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex and reported versus cash capex gap were not reconciled for Hexacom; management said it would revert to the analyst on the difference.
Investment continues in 5G expansion, network modernization, homes and IPTV businesses (per management remarks).
demand_pricing: Mobile ARPU rose to Rs.264; management said the voice-only minimum recharge cohort is very small and would not materially affect headline ARPU.
Northeast weather disruption hurt continuity and recharges in the quarter, with improvement seen versus last quarter.
Competitive intensity described as unchanged; three operators in about half the country and two in the rest.
Home broadband acquisition quality was corrected after low-ARPU commissions and wrong sales practices; claw-back expected to come via higher-value fiber customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were mobile net adds negative and is churn seasonal or tariff-driven, and will it normalize?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a pricing intervention causes temporary churn and the Northeast weather hit continuity hard last quarter; early signs of improvement are visible versus last quarter, so Q3 is to be watched.

qa_highlights.question: Is the postpaid ARPU increase about Rs.50 and will it flow through to ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, broadly Rs.50 flow-through to ARPU, with some possible access charges for international roaming users that may offset part of it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Hexacom's ARPU rise more slowly than Airtel's despite higher data consumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Different customer mix and affordability, a lower base ARPU and Northeast disruption explain the gap; management said results should not be read too literally against Airtel.

qa_highlights.question: Will home broadband net adds, down from over 100,000 to about 70,000 per quarter, accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown is a deliberate correction of past high-competition, low-quality acquisition; growth will be fiber-led and claw-back will come from higher-value customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the minimum recharge or voice-only plans materially affect Hexacom ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the voice-only cohort is very small and shrinking, so the effect on headline ARPU should be insignificant.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a sharp gap between reported and cash capex for Hexacom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have a ready answer and said it would come back on this later.

risks_watch: Mobile churn and negative net adds in Q2; whether continuity recovers in Q3 as management indicated.
Home broadband net adds slowing to about 70,000 per quarter and EBIT margin softness from fiber and CPE investment; management frames this as an investment phase.
Unreconciled gap between reported and cash capex for Hexacom, which management has not yet explained.
Possible reaction of peers to tariff action and Hexacom's ARPU lag versus Airtel given a mix skewed to lower-ARPU customers.
Access charges rising with home broadband growth may keep the margin under pressure.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and explanatory on mobile churn and home broadband, attributing both to a temporary pricing action, seasonality and Northeast weather, while expressing confidence in early Q3 improvement. Management was reluctant to give forward numbers, and deferred the capex reconciliation question.
key_quotes: Whilst I called out Northeast as a reason for having softer net adds because of this, it also impacted existing customers' continuity because those days they could not recharge.
In terms of how we are seeing, we are seeing significant improvement versus what we had in the last quarter. So, let us watch this space for Q3, but we are seeing early signs of improvement.

financial_highlights.change: benefited from one extra day in the quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Homes, offices and other business net adds

growth.why: No formal guidance given; management only noted early churn improvement and possible Northeast recovery into Q3, with no capacity, order or contract numbers behind any growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDAaL margin at 48.6% with access charges expected to stay slightly higher as home broadband grows fast, and fiber/CPE investment pressuring EBIT margin, so no clear margin expansion is signalled.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said investment continues in 5G expansion, network modernization, homes and IPTV, but gave no plant-style capacity numbers or dates, so new capacity is only loosely implied.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Mobile net adds turned negative in Q2 on churn, with early improvement seen versus last quarter and possible Northeast recovery into Q3, while homes/offices/business added 71,000 net adds (down from over 100,000 per quarter).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not framed as a new commitment; the reported versus cash capex gap was unreconciled and management deferred it.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance and declined forward numbers on mobile growth versus Airtel, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Mobile subscriber additions were negative in Q2, Hexacom's mobile revenue grew about 2.7% QoQ versus Airtel's 3.4%, and access charges plus fiber/CPE investment pressure the margin, though management expects churn to improve.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed on the call.

rows.label: Postpaid ARPU uplift of about Rs.50 flowing through
rows.why: Management said the tariff intervention brings roughly Rs.50 postpaid ARPU uplift that should flow through to ARPU, partly offset by possible access charges for international roaming users.

rows.label: Home broadband quality reset with fiber-led growth
rows.why: Home, office and business net adds fell to 71,000 from over 100,000 per quarter after a deliberate correction of low-ARPU acquisitions, with claw-back expected via higher-value fiber customers, but no growth target was given.

tone.note: Management was cautious and explanatory, attributing mobile churn and the home broadband slowdown to a tariff action, seasonality and Northeast weather while seeing early Q3 improvement; analysts pressed on the ARPU gap versus Airtel, churn, and the unreconciled reported versus cash capex.
